text:
Application lifecycle

Because the platform is unidentified, this is a platform-neutral flow; its exact workspace capabilities cannot be verified.

Diagram
flowchart TD
  Idea[Idea or business requirement] --> Define[Define scope requirements and acceptance criteria]
  Define --> Design[Design data workflows interfaces and security]
  Design --> Create[Create or migrate application]
  Create --> Validate[Validate configuration dependencies and tests]
  Validate --> RC1[Package version 1.0 release candidate 1]
  RC1 --> DEV[Deploy release candidate to DEV]
  DEV --> DevPass{DEV validation passed?}
  DevPass -- No --> Fix[Correct defects and package next release candidate or patch]
  Fix --> DEV
  DevPass -- Yes --> QA[Promote same release candidate to QA]
  QA --> QaPass{QA testing and approval passed?}
  QaPass -- No --> Fix
  QaPass -- Yes --> Release[Approve immutable version 1.0]
  Release --> PRD[Deploy version 1.0 to PRD]
  PRD --> DeployPass{Deployment successful?}
  DeployPass -- No --> Rollback[Restore prior approved production version]
  DeployPass -- Yes --> Operate[Operate monitor support and secure]
  Rollback --> Fix
  Operate --> Incident{Critical production incident?}
  Incident -- Yes --> Rollback
  Incident -- No --> Feedback[Collect feedback and enhancement requests]
  Feedback --> Change[Approve and define a later change]
  Change --> Implement[Create change set and implement updates]
  Implement --> V2[Package version 2.0 release candidate 1]
  V2 --> DEV
  Operate --> Needed{Application still needed?}
  Needed -- Yes --> Operate
  Needed -- No --> Retire[Archive required data and decommission]

issues: The platform-neutral caveat is appropriate, but the flow presents non-universal practices as definite: immutable releases, promotion of the same release candidate, automatic rollback for critical incidents, and every later change becoming version 2.0. Generalize these as conditional practices and label the new version as 1.1, 2.0, or another version according to the platform’s versioning policy.

limitations: The platform name and authoritative workspace capabilities were not supplied, so platform-specific stages and availability cannot be confirmed.
